summary: Healthcare knowledge. Content includes clinical guidelines and patient education. The assistant uses it to answer questions about protocols, drugs, dosages and screening.
rationale: Clinical knowledge links treatments to conditions and to the people they suit. Recording which drugs treat or are contraindicated in which conditions, who a drug is recommended for and who approved it lets the assistant answer with the guidance behind it. It records clinical knowledge only, never patient data.

dreaming.instructions:
Record guidance from authoritative sources: clinical protocols, drug information, guidelines, dosages, and approvals or updates. Keep exact doses, units, thresholds, age ranges and dates, and the issuing body. When a guideline replaces an earlier one, record the new one and what it supersedes.

Skip:
- Anecdotal patient outcomes or uncontrolled case reports.
- Unapproved or experimental treatments without trial data.
- Outdated guidelines that have been formally superseded.
- Anything that identifies a patient. Never record it.

facts.description: A screening, diagnostic or treatment protocol, such as "Type 2 diabetes screening recommended annually for BMI >25".
An indication, contraindication or interaction, such as "metformin contraindicated with eGFR below 30 mL/min".
A recommendation from an issuing body, such as "CDC recommends RSV vaccine for adults 60+".
A dose, with units, frequency and population, such as "amoxicillin pediatric dose is 25mg/kg/day divided q12h".
An approval or change with its date, such as "FDA approved semaglutide for obesity treatment in June 2024".

nodes.description: A disease, condition or risk factor.
A medication or vaccine, by generic name.
A group a recommendation applies to, such as adults 60+ or children.
An issuing or approving body, such as the CDC or FDA.

edges.description: The drug is indicated for the condition.
The drug must not be used with the condition.
A guideline recommends the drug for the population.
The body approved the drug, with the indication in the fact.
A protocol recommends screening the population for the condition.
